papers.title: A Reinforcement Learning Method to Navigate SMEFT Operator Space
papers.abstract: In particle physics, discrepancies between experimental measurements and Standard Model (SM) predictions are commonly interpreted within new theoretical models. In this context, the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) provides a general framework encompassing a broad class of models. However, exploring the enormous space of possible SMEFT operators rapidly becomes a challenging combinatorial problem: many operators can contribute simultaneously to different observables, their effects are correlated, and distinct operator combinations can provide comparably good descriptions of the data. In this work, we formulate the exploration of the SMEFT operator space as a sequential decision-making problem using reinforcement learning (RL). Our RL agent employs a lightweight actor-critic architecture with approximately 40K trainable parameters in total. Rather than searching for a single best-fit theory, our method is designed to discover a diverse set of high-quality theory hypotheses. We test the method in a complex phenomenological environment comprising 132 observables across several sectors of particle physics, including 24 measurements that deviate from their SM predictions by more than $1.5\sigma$. We show that the learned RL policy efficiently constructs multi-operator theories that substantially improve the global fit. Comparisons with independent random-subset and random-sequential searches demonstrate the ability of the RL policy to navigate this large combinatorial space. Our results establish RL as a systematic framework for exploring diverse patterns of new physics (NP) interactions within SMEFT.

papers.title: Searching for New Physics with Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Finding new physics (NP) is the fundamental problem in particle physics today. Studying anomalies, i.e., measurements of low-energy observables whose values disagree with the predictions of the Standard Model (SM), is a powerful search strategy. The SM Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) provides a general model-independent framework for parametrizing NP; given some anomalies, it is natural to try to find the SMEFT operator(s) that can explain them. This is a challenging task because (i) the number of SMEFT operators is enormous, and (ii) at loop level there are very complicated correlations among the operators. Analyses by humans typically rely on phenomenological intuition to decide which operators are relevant. This is often biased and does not explore the complete SMEFT operator space. Interestingly, reinforcement learning (RL) techniques excel at tasks that require decision making to achieve their goals. In this paper, we introduce an RL method that can be used to find the SMEFT operators that explain any anomalies. Using some explicit examples, we demonstrate that our RL method can be used to efficiently search for NP at the level of SMEFT. The RL training can be performed efficiently using standard CPU resources, without requiring specialized computing hardware.

papers.title: Combinatorial Residual Network: a decay-chain-aware classifier without explicit jet assignment
papers.abstract: Final states with several jets from the decays of heavy particles pose a combinatorial problem: the jets must be assigned, at least implicitly, to their parent particles. The Combinatorial Residual Network (CoReNet) is a classifier that encodes the assumed decay chain in its architecture, building the event representation level by level along the decay hierarchy and combining all jet assignment hypotheses, evaluated with shared weights, with learned weights. The exchange symmetries of the decay are built in, the network size does not depend on the number of hypotheses, and no generator-level jet assignments are used in training. Developed for the $b\bar{b}b\bar{b}$ final state and used in several CMS searches, CoReNet with 1508 parameters performs well above kinematic baselines on fast-simulated Higgs boson pair production against QCD multijet events and trains in minutes on a single GPU, and its hypothesis weights select the truth-matched jet pairing in most signal events in which it is defined. Since only the encoded decay chain is specific to the final state, we test the construction on $HH \to b\bar{b}W^+W^-$ against semileptonic $t\bar{t}$, where encoding the decay chain of the background as well improves the classification at a cost of about $10^{3}$ parameters. In both final states, CoReNet performs comparably to a state-of-the-art transformer-based network more than two orders of magnitude larger. The implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/cms-cmu/CoReNet.

papers.title: Constraining neutrino masses with localized fast radio bursts: Current bounds and future prospects
papers.abstract:
The dispersion-measure (DM)--redshift relation of fast radio bursts (FRBs) provides independent low-redshift cosmological information for neutrino-mass inference. In this work, we perform joint analyses with cosmic microwave background (CMB) data, using 120 localized FRBs with reliable host-galaxy redshifts and larger mock samples, to investigate the effects of sample size and the dark-energy model on constraints on the sum of neutrino masses, $\sum m_
u$. In the $\Lambda$CDM+$\sum m_
u$ model, CMB+FRB gives $\sum m_
u<0.21\,\mathrm{eV}$, substantially relaxed relative to the current CMB+DESI result. With 1000 simulated events, CMB+FRB1(mock) gives an upper limit of $0.12\,\mathrm{eV}$, which decreases to $0.035\,\mathrm{eV}$ for CMB+FRB2(mock) with 10000 events. The latter is more stringent than the CMB+DESI limit, demonstrating the potential of large localized FRB samples to constrain neutrino mass. When the model is extended to $w_0w_a$CDM+$\sum m_
u$, both the observed and mock samples yield upper limits of approximately $0.3$--$0.4\,\mathrm{eV}$, indicating that the assumed dark-energy model remains a dominant factor in these constraints. As localized FRB samples grow and the modeling of the individual DM contributions becomes more accurate, FRBs may provide further independent low-redshift information for constraining neutrino mass.

papers.title: Nonperturbative lattice simulation of the nucleation rate in thermal first-order phase transitions
papers.abstract: We present a nonperturbative lattice study of vacuum decay through bubble nucleation in a three-dimensional real scalar field theory at finite temperature. The vacuum decay rate is computed by combining an expanded-ensemble multicanonical hybrid Monte Carlo approach, which samples the critical bubble configurations, with real-time Langevin dynamics, which follows the subsequent bubble evolution. We extrapolate the nucleation rate to the continuum limit and compare it with the corresponding one-loop perturbative prediction, finding a discrepancy of about \(8\%\).

papers.title: Black Hole Superradiance and the Gravitational Auger Effect
papers.abstract: Black hole superradiance is a powerful probe of nature's light degrees of freedom. In the vicinity of a spinning black hole, it exponentially amplifies ultralight bosons from vacuum fluctuations to a macroscopic cloud of enormous occupation number. Observational superradiance effects - modified black-hole spins, gravitational-wave and coherent boson emission - are known to depend sensitively on bosonic self-interactions as induced by a quartic, $\lambda \phi^4$. Here we point out that purely gravitational interactions within the cloud significantly modify superradiance dynamics, through an analog of the Auger effect. Moreover, we identify nontrivial evolution of the superradiant levels beyond the first, driven by scattering into even higher levels and their radial overtones. For the QCD axion, the irreducible gravitational coupling rapidly dissipates the first superradiant level after it reaches saturation, through scalar emission and absorption by the black hole, while truncating the growth of higher levels. This can dramatically suppress the observability of continuous gravitational-wave signals or signatures in late binary inspirals. Black hole spin-down remains more robust, but for higher modes begins earlier and proceeds more slowly, requiring revision of existing limits.

papers.title: Triple Exchange at the Cosmological Collider in Closed Form
papers.abstract: Particles with masses near the Hubble scale leave a characteristic pattern in the primordial bispectrum, turning inflation into a cosmological collider. For light fields, where this signal is largest, no closed form is known for the full shape of the quasi-single-field triple exchange. Using Feynman-integral methods, we obtain the first closed-form results, exact in the momenta, as expansions in terms of multiple polylogarithms around the massless and conformally coupled limits. We show that the template used in Planck analyses overestimates the amplitude by up to a factor of 1.8 and underestimates the mass, whereas our new template recovers both, as needed for current and upcoming CMB and galaxy surveys. We also compute the collapsed trispectrum and, combining it with the bispectrum, find that at weak mixing it bounds the self-coupling more tightly.

papers.title: Cosmological Collider Signals from Fermion Bubble Loops with a Chemical Potential
papers.abstract: We present the first systematic analytical calculation of the local and nonlocal cosmological collider (CC) signals generated by massive fermion bubble loops in the presence of an effective chemical potential during inflation. Working in the de Sitter approximation, we investigate the four-point correlator of inflaton perturbations in the single-squeezed limit. By combining CC cutting rules, late-time expansions, and partial Mellin-Barnes (MB) techniques, we derive analytical expressions for both local and nonlocal signals. In particular, we identify two distinct contributions to the local signal, arising from spectrum and integer poles and from ultraviolet poles of the loop-momentum integral. We further investigate the three-point limit, where the separately extracted local and nonlocal contributions develop apparent folded singularities. By reorganizing the MB representation, we demonstrate that these singularities cancel in the complete signal and obtain a convergent double-MB integral suitable for numerical evaluation. Independent calculations using complementary MB representations provide nontrivial consistency checks of our results. We find that the chemical potential can significantly enhance the oscillatory signal while increasing its logarithmic oscillation frequency. Our analytical results provide a foundation for further studies of chemical-potential-enhanced fermionic CC signals, including fermion triangle loops.

papers.title: Pulsar Timing Correlations Induced by Stochastic Spin-2 Ultralight Dark Matter
papers.abstract: Ultralight dark matter (ULDM) can generate time-dependent gravitational perturbations, providing a potential signal for pulsar timing arrays (PTAs). In Galactic halos, the velocity dispersion of ULDM gives rise to finite spatial coherence, which influences the correlations between pulsar timing signals. In this work, we derive the timing-residual cross-correlations induced by rapid metric oscillations of spin-2 ULDM, allowing for general polarization statistics. Under equipartition among the five polarization modes, the intrinsic angular kernel contains monopole and quadrupole components and exhibits an angular profile closely resembling that of spin-1 ULDM, suggesting a potential degeneracy between the two ULDM candidates in PTA observations.

papers.title: Non-Canonical Q-balls in Polyattractor Inflation Models
papers.abstract: We show that Q-balls can exist in supergravity-based polyattractor inflation models that interpolate between $\alpha$-attractor T-models and polynomial attractor models. We consider both the original polyattractor potential and a natural generalisation. We find that Q-balls solutions exist when the model deviates significantly from the T-model $\alpha$-attractor, whereas in the T-model limit no Q-balls exist. These are non-canonical Q-balls due to the non-canonical kinetic term of the complex inflaton field. Such Q-balls could have significant cosmological consequences if they are produced at the end of inflation. In particular, if the global $\mathrm{U}(1)$ symmetry of the supergravity-based polyattractor model is unbroken, the Q-balls can be absolutely stable and could account for dark matter.

papers.title: Minimal Majoron Dark Matter
papers.abstract: We study Majoron dark matter (DM) in its minimal realization, based on the Type-I seesaw framework extended by a SM-singlet complex scalar. Remaining agnostic about the origin and value of the Majoron mass, we evaluate the DM abundance from both the freeze-in and misalignment mechanisms, and identify the viable parameter space consistent with observational constraints. Without fine-tuning of the initial misalignment angle, we find that the Majoron mass is bounded by $m_J \lesssim \mathcal{O}(10)~\mathrm{MeV}$. We also discuss compatibility with thermal leptogenesis. Successful leptogenesis with two right-handed neutrinos favors misalignment-dominated production with the Majoron mass $m_J \lesssim \mathcal{O}(100)~\mathrm{eV}$, while freeze-in dominated production is compatible with leptogenesis only with a mild fine-tuning of the initial misalignment angle, $\theta_i \lesssim \mathcal{O}(0.01)$.

papers.title: Short Gravitational-Wave Transients as Probes of Cosmic Domain Walls
papers.abstract: GW190521 and GW231123 have been reported as short-duration gravitational-wave transients consistent with very massive binary black hole (BBH) coalescences whose inferred parameters, i.e., exceptionally high total masses and spin magnitudes, challenge standard isolated binary stellar evolution. We test a topological dark matter (TDM) interpretation invoking cosmic domain walls by fitting a physically motivated domain wall template to the LIGO Hanford and Livingston strain data. The BBH hypothesis is individually favored, with $\log_{10}\mathcal{B}_{\rm BBH/TDM}=12.2$ and $11.3$ for GW231123 and GW190521, respectively. However, these values are lower than those typically recovered from matched maximum a posteriori BBH waveforms injected into nearby noise segments. We further perform, for the first time, a joint fit in which domain wall signals from a single underlying scalar field are constrained simultaneously by both events. Although not favored over BBH signals, we find the two events are consistent with a common scalar field, with shared TDM parameters agreeing across independent noise realizations and sky locations. We further find that injected TDM transients are systematically recovered under the BBH hypothesis with large spin parameters, revealing a morphological degeneracy that could mask genuine domain wall signals. This analysis demonstrates that multi-event parameter consistency tests provide a new discriminant for domain wall dark matter searches in upcoming observing runs.

papers.title: Fermi-eROSITA cross-correlations suggest annihilation lines of $\sim70$ GeV WIMPs
papers.abstract: The deep potential wells of galaxy clusters provide some of the strongest constraints on the velocity-dependent ($p$-wave) annihilation of weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) dark matter. Cross-correlating high-latitude Fermi-LAT 16.3-year data with the western Galactic hemisphere eROSITA map facilitates high-sensitivity tests. A blind composite matched-filter scan of the cross-correlated spectrum for the $\chi\chi\to\gamma\gamma$, $\gamma Z$, and $\gamma h$ annihilation-line triad of a single WIMP $\chi$ finds $m_\chi c^2\simeq71.9$ and $67.5$ GeV (observer-frame) triads, each with a local $Z$-score $\sim3$ and a (henceforth global) $1.7$-$2.1\sigma$ (trial-corrected), insensitive to details of detrending, sky masks, and filters. The leading nonad (equidistant three triads) corresponds to $66.4$ and $71.9$ GeV cross-annihilating WIMPs ($2.5\sigma$). The leading $\sim72$ GeV triad coincides with the mass implied by interpreting the reported $\sim43.2$ GeV $\gamma$-ray line in three nearby clusters as its $\gamma Z$ channel. At this externally fixed mass, the triad reaches $3.0\sigma$ alone, and $5.1\sigma$ when combined with the reported line ($3.8\sigma$ under alternative assumptions; similar values for the nonad). This triad, absent from the ambient (X-ray-uncorrelated) spectrum, presents in different Galactic sectors, strengthens under cosmological (positive) but not negative redshift broadening $\Delta z$, and peaks at $\Delta z\simeq 0.05$, consistent with galaxy clusters; its two non-$43$ GeV channels reach $2.4\sigma$ by themselves. Measured (not loss-corrected) intrinsic cross sections are a few $10^{-19}$ cm$^3$ s$^{-1}$ for WIMPs tracing the X-ray gas.

papers.title: Dynamical criterion for biased domain-wall formation
papers.abstract: In the presence of a bias term, the conventional condition for forming a domain-wall network is $p_{\rm fv}>p_c\simeq 0.31$, with $p_{\rm fv}/(1-p_{\rm fv})=\exp(-\Delta V(0)/V_b(0))$, where $p_{\rm fv}$ is the false-vacuum fraction immediately after the phase transition, $\Delta V(0)$ is the zero-temperature energy splitting between the false and true vacua and $V_b(0)$ is the zero-temperature barrier height measured from the true vacuum. This criterion, however, cannot be generally valid, since it is insensitive to the dynamics of the phase transition. In this work, we derive a dynamical criterion for domain wall formation in the presence of a bias term. We evaluate $p_{\rm fv}$ at the freeze-out temperature of the false-vacuum correlation volumes $T_{\rm fo}$, obtaining a substantially stricter criterion. The same dynamical picture also yields a necessary consistency condition for applying scaling-regime gravitational-wave estimates, $T_{\rm fo}>T_{\rm ann}$, where $T_{\rm ann}$ is the annihilation temperature inferred from the scaling-regime dynamics.

papers.title: Probing the QCD Conformal Window with Four-Quark Operators
papers.abstract: The infrared fate of QCD-like theories and their conformal window for different numbers or flavours and colour remains an open question with applications ranging from high-energy to condensed-matter systems. A hallmark of phase transitions from a conformal to symmetry breaking phase can be the presence of classically irrelevant operators that provide relevant deformation in the infrared. We investigate this scenario by computing anomalous dimensions of all four-quark operators, with or without chiral symmetry, at four-loop order as well as the dimension-six gluonic operator at three loops in Veneziano QCD. Scaling dimensions are derived in a systematic conformal expansion. These results are improved with various resummation techniques and we estimate their uncertainties. We find no concrete evidence for a composite operator effectively describing a merger with the QCD fixed point.

papers.title: Non-Topological Chiral Anomaly: The Chiral Magnetoelectric Effect
papers.abstract: We derive the chiral anomaly in a thermal medium and show that, in addition to the well-established topological piece, the anomaly acquires a previously overlooked non-topological contribution, relevant for non-gauged axial symmetries. Remarkably, this modification of the continuity equation is independent of the electromagnetic fields, thereby giving rise to novel transport effects in relativistic hydrodynamics. We further propose an experimentally accessible new effect in Weyl semimetals which we call the Chiral Magnetoelectric Effect: an electric field proportional to the magnetic field is generated by the non-topological anomaly, even in the absence of an externally applied electric field. Beyond this concrete prediction, our results establish a broader hydrodynamic framework for non-topological chiral anomalies, opening the door to a range of previously unexplored anomaly-induced transport phenomena across condensed-matter and high-energy systems.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal K-Shape: Reconstructing inhomogeneous condensate profiles on the lattice
papers.abstract: Spatially modulated chiral condensates can affect the phase structure of dense QCD effective models. Understanding such order requires characterizing its real-space structure as well as detecting a modulation. Spatial two-point correlators retain the ensemble-averaged power spectrum but discard relative Fourier phases, leaving the configuration shapes undetermined in general. We propose the Spatiotemporal K-Shape method to extract representative shapes from lattice Monte Carlo ensembles without assuming a functional form. The method extends K-Shape clustering to periodic lattice fields, aligning configurations modulo translations and, optionally, a global sign or phase before extracting cluster centroids. Comparisons across clusterings assess whether one representative shape suffices. Controlled tests recover distinct profiles with identical correlators and separate mixtures of different shapes. Applied to the $(1+1)$-dimensional Gross-Neveu model with $N_f=8$, the method extracts non-sinusoidal profiles with two sign changes at two chemical potentials and separates multiple shape families at a third, where a single centroid is insufficient. Including the discrete chiral sign symmetry in the alignment can fold domain-length fluctuations into an asymmetric centroid without implying a preferred ensemble asymmetry. The method thus complements correlator diagnostics with representative real-space shapes and information on their diversity. The application to the Gross-Neveu model provides a testing ground for configuration-based studies of inhomogeneous order relevant to the QCD phase diagram.

papers.title: $K_1^*(1870)$ and $3S$-$2D$ mixing in the strange meson sector
papers.abstract: Very recently, the BESIII Collaboration reported the first observation of a $J^P=1^-$ strange resonance in the $K\eta'$ system, the $K_1^*(1870)$. We examine whether this state can be accommodated in the kaon meson family. Although it cannot be assigned as a pure $3^3S_1$ or $2^3D_1$ state, we show that it can be described as the lower state of $3S$-$2D$ mixing, whose mass agrees with the measured value, and we predict its higher-mass partner. Using the quark pair creation model, we calculate the OZI-allowed decay properties of both \textcolor{black}{mixed} states; the total decay width of the lower state is consistent with the measured width of the $K_1^*(1870)$. We note that the subordinate $K\eta'$ decay mode of this state appears to contradict its observed $K\eta'$ decay channel, which calls for further study. We further investigate the production of these two states via the $Kp$ reaction, which may provide valuable information for future experimental searches.

papers.title: Confinement--Higgs Complementarity Viewed through Relative Quantum Reference Frames
papers.abstract: We formulate confinement--Higgs complementarity in terms of the relative orientation between two independently constructed quantum reference frames (QRFs): one derived from the gauge field and the other from the scalar field. Exact continuum and lattice identities give a relational interpretation of the scalar--color observables used in recent gauge-fixing-free $SU(2)$ simulations. In particular, we provide a QRF interpretation of the additional gauge-invariant nonlocal separation line obtained from the Cho--Duan--Ge (CDG) reduction reported in lattice simulations of the radially fixed fundamental $SU(2)$ gauge--scalar model. We explain why such a candidate nonlocal boundary is compatible with Fradkin--Shenker continuity and Osterwalder--Seiler analyticity for the appropriate class of local gauge-invariant observables. Separately, we show that a Wilson-rooted control observable admits an exact results at zero plaquette coupling and that it does not cause such a nonlocal separation line.

papers.title: Electromagnetic cross section of charmonium decay
papers.abstract: As an important measurable quantity, the electromagnetic cross sections of charmonium decay in an e+e- collider are valuated for fifteen final states. A general scheme of lS-coupling analysis is adopted for constructing covariant helicity-coupling amplitudes involving two-body decays with arbitrary integer spins. Based on the decay rate, the collision cross section is obtained finally. A number of illustrative examples is worked out to expound and incarnate the general formulas.

papers.title: Fate of chiral and $U(1)_A$ symmetries in hot QCD matter under background magnetic fields
papers.abstract: We summarize our recent lattice QCD study of chiral and singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking in background magnetic fields. The magnetic field explicitly reduces the non-singlet flavor symmetry through the unequal light-quark electric charges. We therefore study two neutral-channel susceptibility differences: $\chi_{\pi^0}-\chi_\sigma$ for chiral symmetry breaking and $\chi_{\pi^0}-\chi_{\delta^0}$ for singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking. The calculation uses fixed-scale $(2+1)$-flavor HISQ ensembles with $m_l=m_s^{\mathrm{phys}}/10$, corresponding to a zero-field pion mass of $M_\pi\simeq220\,\mathrm{MeV}$. Magnetic fields enhance both susceptibility differences at low temperatures. Near the crossover, sufficiently strong fields instead suppress both differences. The suppression sets in at larger magnetic fields and is milder for the singlet-axial susceptibility difference than for the neutral chiral susceptibility difference.

papers.title: Charm quark energy loss fluctuations in clumpy color string medium
papers.abstract: We simulate charm quark propagation through an ensemble of color flux tubes formed between receding color charges in proton-proton collisions. Under the assumption of sharp string boundaries and a localized nature of the overlap regions, high flux tube densities lead to the formation of string clusters. We convert the local energy density of the superposed color field into an effective temperature of an ideal gluon gas and study the dependence of charm energy loss on its spatial inhomogeneities. By comparing different energy-density extraction prescriptions, we show that both elastic and inelastic momentum damping mechanisms are sensitive to the medium properties. However, the collisional channel is an order of magnitude smaller in absolute terms (up to $\sim0.15$~GeV) compared to the radiative loss (up to $\sim1.5$~GeV). Overall, the results demonstrate that the spatial overlap of individual strings generates a complex local energy density pattern, which predominantly governs the medium-induced quenching of charm quarks.

papers.title: Quark + diquark description of nucleon gravitational form factors
papers.abstract: We present parameter-free predictions for the nucleon gravitational form factors (GFFs) using a Poincare-covariant quark+diquark Faddeev equation. We provide the full GFFs ($A$, $J$, $D$, and $\bar{c}$) along with their species decompositions into quark and gluon contributions. Based on the diquark breakdown, we find that while the scalar diquark component dominates the nucleon's energy, spin, and mechanical properties, the axial-vector component plays an indispensable role. The GFF $B(Q^2)$ is predicted to be vanishingly small but nonvanishing at finite $Q^2$; its physical origin is deeply rooted in the nucleon' s internal structure through cancellations in both the diquark content and the $u/d$ flavor sectors. Furthermore, our results for $\bar{c}(Q^2)$ confirm the fundamental symmetry requirements of the approach. Compared with lQCD, our calculated $D$-term and various spatial radii are somewhat smaller in magnitude. This systematic underestimation is primarily driven by the gluon sector and can be attributed to the omission of meson cloud effects, suggesting that these effects impact the gluon distribution more significantly than the quark distribution. Finally, our analysis of the energy density based on two extrapolation schemes reveals that the presence of a negative central energy density is highly model-dependent.

papers.title: Exploring X17 Couplings through Meson Dalitz Decays
papers.abstract: The ATOMKI collaboration has reported anomalous $e^+e^-$ pair production in a series of nuclear transitions, which has been interpreted as a possible signature of a new light boson, X17. Meson Dalitz decays provide a complementary probe of the X17 interaction structure. However, the widely studied vector coupling scenario is in tension with the combined constraints from existing $D^{*0}\to D^0e^+e^-$, $D_s^{*+}\to D_s^+e^+e^-$ measurements and nuclear transition analyses. In this work, we investigate the X17 contributions to meson Dalitz decays within a framework incorporating both vector and axial-vector couplings, employing the Bethe--Salpeter approach to calculate the hadronic transition matrix elements. With $u$ and $d$ quark couplings taken from previous analyses, we identify allowed regions for the charm and strange quark couplings, which require the axial-vector coupling strength $|g_{c,s}^A|\sim10^{-3}$. We obtain four degenerate best-fit solutions, one of which is $(g_c^V,g_c^A,g_s^V,g_s^A)=(8.32,1.09,-2.62,1.36)\times10^{-3}$, and estimate the decay ratio $R^{\mathrm{th}}(D^{*+}\to D^+e^+e^-)$, which significantly exceeds the Standard Model prediction.

papers.title: On reflection positivity of lattice chiral fermions
papers.abstract: We point out that the overlap Weyl fermion, the spacetime lattice realization of a Weyl fermion underlying L\"uscher's construction of lattice chiral gauge theories, is not reflection positive in two and four dimensions at finite lattice spacing. Consequently, the standard Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction does not yield a Hilbert space with a self-adjoint Hamiltonian. In two dimensions, we further show that the overlap Weyl fermion cannot be cut open: the lattice action becomes nonlocal in the presence of a boundary, as expected from the gravitational anomaly of the continuum field theory. By contrast, the overlap Dirac fermion is known to be reflection positive. However, its compact axial symmetry is not invariant under the reflection, whereas a reflection-invariant axial symmetry is noncompact, and both are part of an Onsager algebra.

papers.title: The Future Circular Collider as a photon-photon collider
papers.abstract: The CERN Future Circular Collider (FCC) offers a unique programme of photon-photon interactions in electron-positron, proton-proton, proton-lead, and lead-lead collisions, by exploiting the high-luminosity equivalent photon fluxes associated with the charged beams. Within the equivalent photon approximation, the electromagnetic fields of relativistic charged particles are described in terms of fluxes of quasireal photons. The complementary photon fluxes, energies, and virtualities available across the FCC operation modes provide access to a broad range of two-photon invariant masses and associated physics measurements. Physics opportunities open to study are highlighted, focusing on the exclusive production of C-even resonances, including the SM Higgs boson and searches for spin-0 axion-like (ALPs) and spin-2 graviton-like (GLPs) particles decaying back into photon pairs. These prospective studies demonstrate the potential to observe photon-fusion production of the Higgs boson for all colliding modes, as well as sensitivity to photon-coupled ALPs and GLPs with masses extending up to the kinematic reach of FCC-ee and into the multi-TeV range at FCC-hh collisions, with significant improvements over existing constraints.

papers.title: HVP contributions to the muon anomalous magnetic moment in spacelike and timelike domains
papers.abstract: The hadronic vacuum polarization contributions to the muon anomalous magnetic moment $a^{\text{HVP}}_{\mu}$ in spacelike and timelike domains are recapped. The values of $a^{\text{HVP}}_{\mu}$ assessed within dispersively-improved perturbation theory are reported. The obtained results can be employed in the evaluations of $a^{\text{HVP}}_{\mu}$ in the framework of such methods as lattice studies, MUonE project, and others.

papers.title: Strong Decays of the $2^-$ Heavy-Light Mesons in the Relativistic Bethe-Salpeter Approach
papers.abstract: We present a relativistic study of the mass spectra, the $^1D_2$--$^3D_2$ mixing angles, and the OZI-allowed two-body strong decays of the heavy-light $J^P=2^-$ mesons $D_2$, $D'_2$, $D_{s2}$, $D'_{s2}$, $\bar{B}_2$, $\bar{B}'_2$, $\bar{B}_{s2}$, and $\bar{B}'_{s2}$. The mass spectrum and the meson wave functions are obtained by solving the full instantaneous Bethe--Salpeter (Salpeter) equation, in which the wave-function representations are constructed directly in terms of the $J^P$ quantum numbers rather than the non-relativistic spectroscopic notation ${}^{2S+1}L_J$. For the decay amplitudes we use the partial conservation of the axial-vector current (PCAC) together with the low-energy theorem for the $H\to H'P$ channels, so that the light pseudoscalar meson enters only through its decay constant, and the effective chiral Lagrangian for the $H\to H'V$ channels. The total widths of these mesons are estimated by summing over the partial widths of all OZI-allowed strong decay channels.

papers.title: Lean-Verified No-Go Theorems for $R$-Symmetries and Modular Symmetries in 4D GUTs
papers.abstract: $R$-symmetries are instrumental in supersymmetric model building. However, a no-go theorem restricts us from using them in a large class of four-dimensional (4D) grand unified theories (GUTs). Specifically, it has been shown that a supersymmetric 4D GUT based on SU(5), with finitely many chiral multiplets, cannot be broken spontaneously to the exact minimal supersymmetric standard model (MSSM) while preserving a discrete $\mathbb{Z}_M^R$, with $M \geq 3$, or continuous U(1) $R$-symmetry. We use Lean 4 to formalize this proof. In the process, we identify and close a gap in the general case of the published argument. Further, we discuss the implications for GUT models with modular symmetries. We point out that modular symmetries are inevitably $R$-symmetries in a supersymmetric framework that also describes gravity. At certain critical points in moduli space, discrete $R$-symmetries are linearly realized. In the context of 4D GUTs, the no-go theorem then implies that exotic states become massless at these points, provided the GUT-breaking vacuum preserves these symmetries. In the vicinity of these critical points, these exotics are parametrically light, which may spoil gauge coupling unification.

papers.title: General Formulation of Covariant Tensor Amplitudes for Purely Hadronic and Single-photon Radiative Cascade Decays
papers.abstract:
We present a unified method for generating Lorentz-covariant partial-wave amplitudes for multi-body purely hadronic and single-photon radiative cascade decays within the covariant $L$-$S$ tensor formalism. Based on the structural decoupling of external polarization wave functions, complex coupling parameters, and the core covariant amplitude tensor $U$, we establish a hierarchical vertex contraction procedure that explicitly incorporates intermediate-state cascade bridge projection operators $P^{(J_i)}(p_i)$ and parent-frame definite-spin projection operators $P^{(S_{BC})}(p_A)$. This rigorous treatment guarantees the Rarita-Schwinger symmetry, tracelessness, and transversality conditions across different reference frames, fundamentally eliminating the unphysical longitudinal and trace contaminations induced by Lorentz boosts in cascade decays. Furthermore, we formulate a general covariant tensor representation for single-photon radiative decays $A(J_M) 	o \gamma + X(J_X)$ that strictly satisfies photon gauge invariance ($q^\lambda V_{\dots\lambda\dots} = 0$) in the Lorenz gauge. Built upon normal- and anomalous-parity fundamental transverse tensors ($K_{\mu
u}$ and $S_{\mu
u}$), universal recursive formulas are derived via the systematic replacement $g_{\mu
u} 	o q_\mu p_{A
u}$, accompanied by exact rules for matching the orbital angular momentum ranks of Blatt-Weisskopf centrifugal barrier factors $B_{L_{	ext{rad}}}$ and a spectator index pass-through mechanism for the photon polarization index.
